title: Verification impact DAG routing
outOfScope: Scheduler, retry controller, Work Item execution, agent execution, receipt reuse/cache implementation, provider configuration, release publication, tags, and any claim that a graph schedules work.

sources.reason: Task 8 no-reuse decision and future binding requirements.
Current Fast, Finish, and Hosted proof layers.

riskAssessment.reason: An incomplete graph or stale receipt state could misrepresent which required verification proof remains necessary.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: A bounded declarative evaluator and tests are specified.

preReviewWarnings: Review that graph output is observational and does not schedule or skip verification.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A declarative graph reports required nodes, dependency edges, parallelizable groups, and proof layers for Light, Standard, Strict, and Release without executing or scheduling work.
A graph that omits a required final-proof node is rejected, and any changed receipt binding makes the matching node invalidated rather than cached.
ai_verify exposes the selected graph as observation while retaining existing verification execution behavior.
Focused graph and verification-evidence tests plus governed lifecycle checks are recorded.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: Verification selection currently has small policy helpers but no declarative, inspectable graph that distinguishes required proof from parallelizable or invalidated nodes.
constraints: Evaluator output is deterministic and observational.
Binding mismatch leaves a required node invalidated.
Graph evaluation has no scheduler, retry, provider, or agent side effect.
The change remains limited to this Work Item lifecycle.
intent.rationale: A pure graph makes verification dependencies and invalidation visible without confusing evidence planning with execution.
